infra.explorer.ask.screen: explain this screen and what it shows
infra.explorer.denied: This account has no permission for that action
infra.explorer.deniedNote: The active account lacks permission for some actions — those buttons were hidden
infra.explorer.dock.done: Infra session pinned to the bottom-right corner
infra.explorer.search.localOnly: The search box only filters the rows already LOADED above, it does not scan the whole account — press “Load more” to widen the range.
infra.explorer.pinned.title: Pinned services
infra.explorer.pinned.empty: No pinned service yet. Open “All services” and use the pin button on a card.
infra.explorer.pinned.resize: Drag to resize the services column
infra.explorer.side.title: Services
infra.explorer.services.title: Service catalog
infra.explorer.services.offline: Not connected to the AWOG engine, and the service catalog lives there — so there is nothing to show yet. The catalog only appears when this page runs inside the AWOG app (Electron), not when you open localhost directly in a browser.
infra.explorer.services.failed: The AWOG engine did not return the service catalog.
infra.explorer.services.mock: Showing a SAMPLE CATALOG — this page is open in a browser, so it cannot reach the AWOG engine. The service list and links are sample data for reviewing the UI, NOT your AWS account. Run inside the AWOG app for real data.
infra.explorer.support.hint.full: AWOG has its own screen for this service: resource table, detail view, and working action buttons (start, stop, delete… depending on the service).
infra.explorer.support.hint.list: AWOG can only list them for you to read — there are no action buttons.
infra.explorer.support.hint.console: AWOG has no screen for this service yet. The ↗ button opens it in the AWS Console, or ask the agent to run the CLI for you.
infra.explorer.levels.title: The three support labels
infra.explorer.levels.intro: Each service card carries a label saying what you can do with that service in AWOG — so you know before you click, instead of finding out after.
infra.explorer.confirm.list: This command only reads data, but reads can still cost money by volume.
infra.explorer.confirm.detail: This command only reads one object's details.
infra.explorer.toast.noConsole: This service has no Console link yet
infra.explorer.col.name: Name
infra.explorer.about.s3: Object storage. Buckets are global; objects live inside a bucket under a key.
infra.explorer.about.ec2: Virtual servers. Stopping drops the compute charge but keeps the disk; terminating is irreversible.
infra.explorer.about.lambda: Event-driven functions — you only pay when they run.
infra.explorer.about.dynamodb: Key-value database with no servers to manage.
infra.explorer.about.sqs: Message queues that buffer between producer and consumer.
infra.explorer.about.sns: A publish channel that fans a message out to many subscribers.
infra.explorer.about.ecr: Container image registry for this account.
infra.explorer.about.secretsmanager: Encrypted secret store. This screen shows NAMES only, never values.
infra.explorer.about.cloudformation: Infrastructure as code: one stack is a set of resources created together.
infra.explorer.about.route53: Domains and DNS records. A global service — it belongs to no region.
infra.explorer.about.ecs: Container clusters. A cluster only holds things; open its services/tasks to see work.
infra.explorer.about.eks: AWS-managed Kubernetes. AWOG's Kubernetes screen reads your own kubeconfig.
infra.explorer.about.batch: Run batch jobs on AWS-provisioned compute.
infra.explorer.about.apprunner: Run containers/web apps without managing servers.
infra.explorer.about.efs: Shared network file system for many machines.
infra.explorer.about.elasticache: Managed Redis, Valkey or Memcached for caching.
infra.explorer.about.vpc: Your private network: subnets, routes, internet gateways.
infra.explorer.about.elbv2: Load balancers in front of your applications.
infra.explorer.about.cloudfront: CDN that moves content close to users. Its certificates must live in us-east-1.
infra.explorer.about.apigateway: HTTP/WebSocket front door in front of Lambda or a service.
infra.explorer.about.natgateway: Internet egress for private subnets. Billed per hour and per gigabyte.
infra.explorer.about.acm: TLS certificates. Certificates used by CloudFront must be created in us-east-1.
infra.explorer.about.codebuild: Runs build/test steps on temporary infrastructure.
infra.explorer.about.cloudwatch: Metrics, logs and alarms. AWOG has a dedicated Logs screen for it.
infra.explorer.about.cloudtrail: Audit trail of every API call in the account.
infra.explorer.about.xray: Trace one request as it crosses several services.
infra.explorer.about.iam: Users, roles and permissions. A global service.
infra.explorer.about.waf: Application-layer firewall in front of CloudFront or an ALB.
infra.explorer.about.stepfunctions: State machines: chain steps into one flow.
infra.explorer.about.budgets: Budgets and alerts when you exceed them.
infra.explorer.about.terraform: Terraform workspace state — see the Overview tab.
infra.explorer.about.kubernetes: Reads the kubeconfig on your machine and lists clusters/workloads.
infra.explorer.about.lightsail: Small servers at a flat monthly price — simpler than EC2, with fewer knobs.
infra.explorer.about.elasticbeanstalk: Upload code and AWS builds the servers, load balancer and scaling.
infra.explorer.about.memorydb: Durable Redis/Valkey — cache-fast, but the data survives a restart.
infra.explorer.about.neptune: Graph database for deeply connected data.
infra.explorer.about.backup: Central backup plans across services, all in one place.
infra.explorer.about.fsx: Shared file systems: Windows, Lustre, NetApp.
infra.explorer.about.datasync: Moves bulk data between servers, S3 and EFS.
infra.explorer.about.transfer: SFTP/FTPS straight into S3 or EFS, no server to run.
infra.explorer.about.dms: Moves data between databases, even across engines.
infra.explorer.about.globalaccelerator: Routes users to the nearest copy over AWS's own network, not the internet.
infra.explorer.about.route53resolver: DNS for your VPC: outbound and inbound.
infra.explorer.about.networkmanager: One view of the whole network: VPCs, links, sites.
infra.explorer.about.cloudmap: Service registry so services can find each other.
infra.explorer.about.appmesh: Service mesh: routing and observability between containers.
infra.explorer.about.codedeploy: Rolls a new version onto servers or containers step by step.
infra.explorer.about.codeartifact: Private package registry for npm, pip, Maven…
infra.explorer.about.cloud9: Browser IDE that already has the account's AWS permissions.
infra.explorer.about.cloudshell: An AWS terminal in the browser, CLI pre-installed.
infra.explorer.about.servicecatalog: Pre-approved products people in your org can self-serve.
infra.explorer.about.prometheus: Collects and stores Prometheus metrics for you.
infra.explorer.about.devops-guru: ML that flags anomalies and suggests the cause.
infra.explorer.about.health: AWS incidents and maintenance that touch this account.
infra.explorer.about.chatbot: Sends alerts into Slack/Teams instead of email only.
infra.explorer.about.resource-explorer: Search one resource across every region and service.
infra.explorer.about.singlesignon: Single sign-on for people in your organization.
infra.explorer.about.organizations: Groups AWS accounts into one tree with shared policies.
infra.explorer.about.controltower: Sets up a landing zone the AWS-recommended way.
infra.explorer.about.config: Records what changed, when, and whether it broke a rule.
infra.explorer.about.guardduty: Detects suspicious activity from your account's logs.
infra.explorer.about.securityhub: Aggregates security findings into one scoreboard.
infra.explorer.about.detective: Investigates who called what, from where, after an alert.
infra.explorer.about.macie: Finds sensitive data sitting in S3.
infra.explorer.about.access-analyzer: Points out access that is open to the outside without you knowing.
infra.explorer.about.ram: Shares resources with other accounts in your org.
infra.explorer.about.artifact: Downloads AWS compliance reports and agreements.
infra.explorer.about.servicequotas: Shows quota usage and requests increases.
infra.explorer.about.scheduler: Cron-style schedules without a server to run them.
infra.explorer.about.firehose: Streams data straight into S3, Redshift or OpenSearch.
infra.explorer.about.appflow: Syncs data between SaaS apps (Salesforce, Slack…) and AWS.
infra.explorer.about.trustedadvisor: Checklist of cost, security and quota issues worth fixing.
infra.explorer.about.compute-optimizer: Recommends better sizes for EC2, Lambda and EBS.
infra.explorer.about.athena: Runs SQL over data in S3 with no servers.
infra.explorer.about.glue: Batch data transformation plus the data catalog.
infra.explorer.about.emr: Runs Spark/Hadoop clusters that disappear when the job is done.
infra.explorer.about.redshift: Data warehouse for analytics over large datasets.
infra.explorer.about.opensearch: Full-text search and log analytics, the open fork of Elasticsearch.
infra.explorer.about.lakeformation: Fine-grained permissions for a data lake on S3.
infra.explorer.about.bedrock: Calls foundation models from several vendors through one API.
infra.explorer.about.textract: Pulls text and tables out of images/PDFs.
infra.explorer.about.comprehend: Classifies text, extracts entities and sentiment.
infra.explorer.about.rekognition: Detects objects, faces and text in images and video.
infra.explorer.consequence.start: The instance starts running and begins billing by the hour.
infra.explorer.consequence.stop: The instance stops. The disk stays and keeps billing, the compute part does not.
infra.explorer.consequence.reboot: The instance restarts. Everything running on it is interrupted.
infra.explorer.consequence.terminate: The instance is deleted permanently, along with its attached disks. Unrecoverable.
infra.explorer.consequence.download: The file is downloaded to this machine.
infra.explorer.consequence.deleteObject: The object is removed from the bucket. Unrecoverable.
infra.explorer.consequence.createBucket: A new bucket is created with the name you type. Bucket names are unique worldwide.
infra.explorer.consequence.createFolder: An empty key ending in “/” is created — S3 has no real folders, this only sets a prefix.
infra.explorer.consequence.upload: The local file is uploaded into this bucket.
infra.explorer.consequence.presign: A signed URL is created, valid for 15 minutes and NOT written to the audit log.
infra.explorer.error.badJson: The CLI output is not JSON — unreadable.
infra.explorer.error.cli: The command failed without saying anything more.
infra.explorer.error.noAction: That action is not declared on this view.
infra.explorer.error.typeName: The typed name does not match — nothing was run.
infra.explorer.about.apigatewayv2: HTTP and WebSocket APIs — the newer API Gateway flavour.
infra.explorer.consequence.invalidate: CloudFront re-fetches these paths from your origin on the next request, so the first requests afterwards are slower. Beyond 1000 paths a month AWS charges per path.
infra.explorer.consequence.viewInvalidat: Opens the invalidation history of this distribution. Nothing is changed.
infra.explorer.consequence.viewRecords: Opens the DNS records of this hosted zone. Nothing is changed.
infra.explorer.notice.acmRegion: ACM is a regional service, and CloudFront only accepts certificates created in us-east-1 — a certificate for a load balancer must sit in that load balancer's region. If this table is empty, check the region selector above before concluding you have no certificates.
infra.explorer.notice.apigatewayRestOnly: This table lists REST APIs (API Gateway v1) only. HTTP and WebSocket APIs live under “API Gateway — HTTP/WebSocket APIs”, in the left column once API Gateway is pinned.
infra.explorer.error.navigationOnly: That action opens another screen — it runs no command.
